text: Rohan, this month we'll be scheduling a structured cardiovascular stress test. It's designed to measure your aerobic capacity, recovery kinetics, and efficiency after six months of training.
Sounds good. What does the test involve exactly? Recovery 69% this morning.
It's a treadmill-based graded protocol. We'll start at walking pace and increase intensity every 3 minutes until you reach 85% of max heart rate. We'll monitor HRV, lactate, and recovery slope.
Completed the stress test this morning. Max HR reached 158 bpm. Recovery HR dropped by 25 bpm within the first 2 minutes after stopping. Recovery score 71%.
That's an excellent recovery slope. It shows your cardiovascular system is adapting well. VO2 estimate has improved by nearly 12% since baseline.
We'll also run a blood panel this week to confirm internal markers are aligning with your performance gains.
Your mid-month panel is back. ApoB has dropped another 8 points, hs-CRP is within optimal range, and fasting glucose has stabilized further.
That's encouraging. So the endurance and intervals haven't increased inflammation? Recovery 68% today.
Correct. Your markers are stable. This shows the training load is balanced well with your recovery practices.
From a nutrition side, we'll continue focusing on omega-3s and a plant-forward approach to sustain these improvements.
BP this week averaged 121/75. HRV is steady at 60-62ms. Energy levels feel more consistent even with work stress. Recovery averaging 70%.
That consistency is a marker of resilience. Stress test + biomarkers together confirm your system is stronger and more adaptive than at onboarding.

Month 7 summary: stress test shows strong cardiovascular gains, biomarkers are aligned, and resilience under work stress has improved. November will be about consolidating habits and preparing for your first annual screening.
